scope: Approval-only reconciliation of an exactly bound durable intent, signed transaction and confirmed canonical state. Independent local orchestration, signed-message, read-only transport and adapter tests; no live-scenario or browser mutation.

coverage: Exact first and second revised approvals reconcile once without outbound effects
Repeated and concurrent checks, restart before/after recovery and original request retry preserve one event and approval identity
Unseen, unconfirmed, failed, rate-limited, stale-snapshot and signature-mismatch failures retain accounting state, operation lock and durable intent
Illegal settlement delta and unsupported credit intent cannot reach approval verifier
Final persistence failure retains both in-memory and durable operation lock
Current scenario must match the durable intent before-state
Public unresolved metadata excludes private snapshots, signed bytes and keys
A payment queued behind first-approval recovery cannot bypass the second approval
Independently constructed signed approval matches reconstructed compiled message despite fee-payer privilege normalization
Saved actor, action, revision, scenario account, prepared kind, recipient and fingerprint mismatches reject
Wrong program/tag/revision/obligation/revision account, extra account, extra transfer, second business instruction, wrong compute instruction and wrong fee payer reject
Intended-after mutations to history, settlement, extra approver, amount, recipient, event count, reused event ID and event/approval times reject
Exact signed-byte identity is inspected using confirmed base64 getTransaction only
Tampered signature, hash, blockhash and serialized bytes reject before RPC
Unseen, failed, different-wire, missing metadata/error, invalid slot and unknown encoding reject
429 inspection remains bounded and never uses a send RPC
Durable preparation failure aborts before transaction broadcast
Exact successful approval snapshot uses confirmed minimum context slot at least the confirmed transaction slot on every program-account read
Independent spies reject any signing or sending during reconciliation
Missing expected approval, additional later approval, advanced revision, paid state, expired readiness, changed amount and changed credit digest reject despite a successful exact signature
Auxiliary proof persistence failure does not poison deduplication; retry persists exactly one proof

findings.issue: Adapter appended a recovery proof to its in-memory array before awaiting the proof-file write. A failed write left an in-memory signature that could suppress persistence on a later status check and permit clearing the authoritative lock without a durable auxiliary proof.
findings.resolution: Parent changed normal-effect and reconciliation proof handling to construct a candidate list, await the atomic file write, and only then replace the in-memory list.
findings.verification: The independent auxiliary-proof failure test forces the first write to fail, confirms the in-memory list remains empty, retries successfully, verifies the durable signature and checks repeated reconciliation leaves one proof.

conclusion: No remaining blocking finding was identified within the accepted approval-only recovery scope at completion of this bounded review.
limits: Fixtures use temporary synthetic keys/state, independently constructed signed transactions, mocked read-only RPC records and program accounts. They do not constitute a new compiled SBF audit or independent live devnet observation.
Engine orchestration cases intentionally mock the verifier; message, transport and adapter cases separately validate the proof boundaries.
Automatic credit, payment, reset, capture and failed stale-replay recovery remains unsupported and locked, as required by the accepted decision.

Parent owns the controller-attested legacy-journal binding, real interrupted-scenario recovery, control-plane mutations, build and final remote verification. This tester did not mutate the live scenario or perform those operations.

Browser wording, desktop/mobile layout and accountant workflow completion belong to a separate fresh-context evaluator; this source-aware report does not claim blind usability validation or production accounting acceptance.
The full 109-test count includes other authors' suites; only the 65 cases in the four listed recovery files are attributed to this independent recovery assignment.
